newsitem.title: USA: Tiger Woods craze driving golf industry growth.
newsitem.headline: Tiger Woods craze driving golf industry growth.

text.p: Golf sensation Tiger Woods is driving hoards of young people to take up the sport and adding to the momentum in the growing golf business, according to the chairman of Family Golf Centers Inc.

"Ever since he became a pro, we've seen a 50 percent increase of young people taking classes at our junior clinics, and they come from all ethnic backgrounds. It's phenomenal," said Dominic Chang, whose company owns and operates golf courses and driving ranges.

The appeal of Woods, whose mother is Thai and whose father is black, appears to cut across gender as well as ethnic lines. Chang said both boys and girls are showing up in droves for golf lessons, a healthy sign for the future of the industry.
A new customer demographic has emerged, which Chang calls '3-setters' -- young people who buy three sets of golf clubs over a period of just a few years.

"They get their first set in early adolescence when they start, and after two or three years they buy another set as a teenager. Then in high school and college they will want an even better set ... It's a phenomenon we intend to cultivate," Chang said on a conference call after the release of his company's fourth quarter earnings.

He said Family Golf is also seeing far more women sign up for lessons, and demand for lessons is up overall. Individual half-hour lessons at the company's four New York State facilities grew a whopping 53 percent in 1996, he said.
Chang said his company is in negotiations for an acquisition in New York City, but he did not disclose details, saying not all the approvals are yet in hand.
"It's very exciting. They (New York City) have probably five million people and no driving range there at all," Chang said.

Tiger Woods, 21, was three times the U.S. amateur champion before he dropped out of Stanford University to become a professional golfer. He immediately landed a $60 million endorsement contract with Nike Inc and quickly won two big tournaments -- the Las Vegas Invitational and the Walt Disney World Classic -- in one of the most impressive debuts in the history of the Professional Golf Association Tour.
